question: outcome_summary
answer: The study demonstrated significant improvements in self-efficacy and attitudes towards suicide prevention among nursing staff following the training program. Self-efficacy scores increased from a pre-test mean of 38.13 to a post-test mean of 51.42, indicating enhanced confidence in managing suicidal behaviors. Attitude scores also improved, with pre-test scores rising from 57.05 to 64.89, reflecting a more positive outlook on suicide prevention. The training was effective across all age groups and experience levels, although some attitude components showed no substantial changes.

question: demographics_summary
answer: A total of seventy-two nursing staff participated in the study, with a mean age of 33.85 years (± 9.22). The age distribution revealed that 35 individuals (48.6%) were under 30 years, 24 individuals (33.3%) were between 31 and 40 years, and 13 individuals (18.1%) were above 40 years. A significant majority were married, accounting for 54 individuals (75%).
